items.event_title: Amazon seeks to offload about $8B of Nvidia AI chips to investors via SPV
items.news_summary: Reuters, citing the Financial Times, reported Amazon is working to transfer roughly $8 billion of Nvidia Grace Blackwell AI chips already installed across more than a dozen U.S. data centers into a special-purpose vehicle, lease the chips back, and finance the SPV with debt while potentially offering investors up to a 10% equity stake.
items.investor_materiality: Very high read-through to AI capex financing, hyperscaler balance-sheet strategy and Nvidia GPU asset values. It suggests AI infrastructure is increasingly being financed with structured capital rather than sitting entirely on hyperscaler balance sheets.
items.selection_reason: Fresh multi-billion-dollar financing structure involving Amazon and Nvidia with direct implications for AI capex economics and credit markets.
source_references: Reuters 2026-10-02: Amazon seeks to offload $8 billion of Nvidia chips to investors, FT reports
items.source_quality_note: Reuters report citing Financial Times; Amazon and Nvidia had not immediately commented, so transaction details remain reported rather than company-confirmed.

items.event_title: AI spending boom lifts factory activity across Europe and Asia
items.news_summary: Reuters reported September factory activity strengthened across parts of Europe and Asia as AI-related capital-goods demand supported manufacturing. Euro-zone PMI reached 52.9, Taiwan PMI rose to 56.7, and South Korea recorded its fastest export growth in more than 15 years, while Japan remained weaker.
items.investor_materiality: Medium-high confirmation that AI capex is feeding into physical manufacturing and export demand rather than remaining only a stock-market narrative.
items.selection_reason: Fresh cross-region macro data directly tying AI spending to real-economy manufacturing activity.

items.event_title: French supercomputer maker Bull doubles production capacity for Europe's AI buildout
items.news_summary: Reuters reported state-owned Bull doubled output capacity at its Angers factory from 6 to 12 racks per month, with potential to reach 24 by 2027, as Europe deploys billions of euros toward sovereign AI and supercomputing capacity. Nvidia NVL systems are also set to be partly assembled in Europe through a Foxconn partnership.
items.investor_materiality: Medium-high read-through to European sovereign AI spending, Nvidia rack deployments and local AI infrastructure supply chains.
items.selection_reason: Fresh capacity expansion tied directly to Europe's sovereign-compute push and Nvidia systems.
source_references: Reuters 2026-10-01: French supercomputer maker Bull doubles output to boost Europe's AI ambitions
items.source_quality_note: Reuters reporting with company/factory and EU investment details; high quality.
